Published: 12.07.2018 

# Thirty-Two Senators Now Cosponsoring First Step Act

Daines, Smith, Tillis, Bennet Endorse Criminal Justice Reform Package

**WASHINGTON** – Senators Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) and Michael Bennet (D-Colo.) have joined the growing list of cosponsors of the new _[First Step Act](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/press/rep/releases/senators-unveil-revised-bipartisan-prison-sentencing-legislation)_(S.3649). A balanced bipartisan crowd of 30 senators have now sponsored the legislation—endorsed by the President—to reform America’s criminal justice system.

_“Meth use has skyrocketed in Montana. We need to make sure we have every tool available to fight against an epidemic that is tearing families apart and increasing violent crimes in our state. I’m glad to have worked to keep high level meth dealers and other hardened criminals off our streets. The First Step Act also uses proven tools to reduce recidivism to help protect Montana families and communities and save taxpayer dollars. I’m happy to cosponsor the bill,” **Daines said.**_

_“I am proud to join my colleagues in cosponsoring the First Step Act, which will make meaningful changes to our federal criminal justice system to reduce disparities in sentencing, improve the fairness and effectiveness of our criminal justice system, and keep our communities safe. This bill represents a historic opportunity to implement evidence-based policy reforms and strengthen the public’s faith in the integrity of our criminal justice system,” **Smith said.**_

_“One of my proudest moments as Speaker of the House in North Carolina was passing the Justice Reinvestment Act, a landmark state law that implemented a number of commonsense, bipartisan reforms that resulted in reduced crime, fewer prisons, and lower recidivism rates in North Carolina. With the First Step Act, we now have the opportunity to implement similar, once in a generation criminal justice reforms at the federal level. These commonsense reforms will make our communities safer, modernize outdated and unfair sentencing laws and provide federal prisoners with the tools they need to return to society and become productive members of our communities. Chairman Grassley’s leadership has been unparalleled, and his relentless efforts to forge a bipartisan compromise on such a difficult issue should be applauded. I look forward to working with Chairman Grassley to build support for the First Step Act,” **Tillis said.**_

_“This bill is the result of principled bipartisan compromise—regrettably a rare sight in today’s Senate—that has earned broad support from both the law enforcement community and criminal justice reform advocates. These reforms are a first step in a longer effort to reduce mass incarceration and restore faith in our justice system. Leader McConnell should schedule a vote on the Senate floor before the end of the year,” **Bennet said.**_

Cosponsors of the _First Step Act_ include:

2.Dick Durbin (D-Ill.)

[Here is a full list of cosponsors and endorsements from other organizations](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/download/first-step-act-s3649_-supporters).  

The _First Step Act_ is backed by President Trump and endorsed by a number of law enforcement groups, including the [nation’s largest police group](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/download/fraternal-order-of-police-endorses-first-step-act). It’s [also now supported by 172 former federal prosecutors](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/download/2018-11-26-172-former-federal-prosecutors_-support-first-step-act) including two former Republican U.S. attorneys general, two former deputy attorneys general and a former director of the FBI along with [sheriffs from 34 states](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/download/2018-11-29-56-sheriffs_-support-first-step-act) across the country. The National Governor’s Association, which represents the governors of all 50 states, also [praised the bill](https://www.nga.org/news/press-releases/governors-first-step-act-deserves-a-vote-this-congress/). And a broad coalition of conservative, progressive, and faith groups also support the _First Step Act_.

The bill has also been endorsed by the oft-divergent editorial boards of the _[New York Times and the Wall Street Journal](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/press/rep/releases/wall-street-journal-new-york-times-praise-trump-backed-first-step-act)_, as well as by the editorial boards of _[USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/2018/12/03/first-step-act-let-senate-vote-prison-sentences-editorials-debates/2143884002/),_ _[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2018-12-07/first-step-act-mitch-mcconnell-shouldn-t-block-sentencing-reform)_ and the _[Houston Chronicle](https://www.chron.com/opinion/editorials/article/Cornyn-faces-leadership-test-as-Senate-confronts-13410594.php)_.

_“One of my proudest moments as Speaker of the House in North Carolina was passing the Justice Reinvestment Act, a landmark state law that implemented a number of commonsense, bipartisan reforms that resulted in reduced crime, fewer prisons, and lower recidivism rates in North Carolina. With the First Step Act, we now have the opportunity to implement similar, once in a generation criminal justice reforms at the federal level. These commonsense reforms will make our communities safer, modernize outdated and unfair sentencing laws and provide federal prisoners with the tools they need to return to society and become productive members of our communities. Chairman Grassley’s leadership has been unparalleled, and his relentless efforts to forge a bipartisan compromise on such a difficult issue should be applauded. I look forward to working with Chairman Grassley to build support for the First Step Act,” **Tillis said.**_

_“This bill is the result of principled bipartisan compromise—regrettably a rare sight in today’s Senate—that has earned broad support from both the law enforcement community and criminal justice reform advocates. These reforms are a first step in a longer effort to reduce mass incarceration and restore faith in our justice system. Leader McConnell should schedule a vote on the Senate floor before the end of the year,” **Bennet said.**_

**Christopher Scott  Murphy** (born August 3, 1973) is an American lawyer, author, and politician serving since 2013 as the [junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seniority_in_the_United_States_Senate "Seniority in the United States Senate")[United States senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"). A member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), he served from 2007 to 2013 in the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"), representing [Connecticut's 5th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut's_5th_congressional_district "Connecticut's 5th congressional district").

Before being elected to Congress, Murphy was a member of both chambers of the [Connecticut General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_General_Assembly "Connecticut General Assembly"), serving two terms each in the [Connecticut House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_House_of_Representatives "Connecticut House of Representatives") (1999–2003) and the [Connecticut Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Senate "Connecticut Senate") (2003–2007).

Murphy ran for the U.S. Senate in [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_Senate_election_in_Connecticut "2012 United States Senate election in Connecticut") after longtime incumbent [Joe Lieberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman "Joe Lieberman") announced his retirement. Murphy defeated former Connecticut secretary of state [Susan Bysiewicz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Bysiewicz "Susan Bysiewicz") in the Democratic primary and [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") nominee [Linda McMahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_McMahon "Linda McMahon") in the general election. Aged 39 at the time, Murphy was the youngest senator of the [113th Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/113th_United_States_Congress "113th United States Congress"). He was reelected in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_United_States_Senate_election_in_Connecticut "2018 United States Senate election in Connecticut") and [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_Senate_election_in_Connecticut "2024 United States Senate election in Connecticut").

## Early life, education, and early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life, education, and early career")]

Murphy was born on August 3, 1973, in [White Plains, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Plains,_New_York "White Plains, New York"), to Catherine A. (née Lewczyk) and Scott L. Murphy.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-1) He is of Irish and Polish descent.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-2) Murphy's father is a corporate lawyer who served as the managing partner of Shipman & Goodwin, a [Hartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford,_Connecticut "Hartford, Connecticut") law firm, and his mother is a retired [ESL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESL "ESL") teacher at Hanmer Elementary School in [Wethersfield, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wethersfield,_Connecticut "Wethersfield, Connecticut"). Murphy has two younger siblings.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-3)

Murphy is a graduate of [Wethersfield High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wethersfield_High_School_(Connecticut) "Wethersfield High School (Connecticut)"). He received his Bachelor of Arts degree from his father's alma mater, [Williams College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_College "Williams College"), and his [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") degree from the [University of Connecticut School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Connecticut_School_of_Law "University of Connecticut School of Law"). Murphy spent his junior year studying abroad at [Exeter College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exeter_College,_Oxford "Exeter College, Oxford") through the [Williams-Exeter Programme at Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams-Exeter_Programme_at_Oxford_(WEPO) "Williams-Exeter Programme at Oxford (WEPO)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-4) On May 19, 2013, Murphy received an [honorary Doctor of Humane Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_degree "Honorary degree") degree from the [University of New Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_Haven "University of New Haven").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-5) He was a student body president and founded his high school's [Young Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Democrats_of_America "Young Democrats of America").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:11-6)

In 1996, Murphy managed Charlotte Koskoff's unsuccessful campaign for the House of Representatives against [Nancy Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Johnson "Nancy Johnson"); a decade later, Murphy himself unseated Johnson. From 1997 to 1998, Murphy worked for [Connecticut State Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_State_Senate "Connecticut State Senate") Majority Leader [George Jepsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Jepsen "George Jepsen"). Murphy was first elected to office in 1997, when he won a seat on [Southington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southington,_Connecticut "Southington, Connecticut")'s [planning and zoning commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planning_and_zoning_commission "Planning and zoning commission").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-7)

## Connecticut House of Representatives (1999–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Connecticut House of Representatives (1999–2003)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Chris_Murphy_in_1996.jpg/330px-Chris_Murphy_in_1996.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chris_Murphy_in_1996.jpg)

Murphy on election night, 1996

### Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Elections")]

In 1998, at age 25, Murphy challenged 14-year incumbent Republican State Representative Angelo Fusco. Murphy was endorsed by the six largest labor unions in the state. The CT Employees Independent Union endorsed Murphy, the first time the union had endorsed Fusco's opponent.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-8) Fusco described himself as a union member, an environmentalist, and a moderate.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-9) Murphy defeated Fusco, 55%–45%.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-10) In 2000, he was reelected, defeating Barbara Morelli, 68%–32%.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-11)

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tenure")]

As early as March 1999, Murphy criticized U.S. Congresswoman [Nancy Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Johnson "Nancy Johnson")'s vote to [impeach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Bill_Clinton "Impeachment of Bill Clinton") President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-12) In 2001, he co-sponsored a bill to eliminate child poverty.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-13) He proposed legislation to give free tuition to students of the state's community-technical colleges.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-14) He proposed legislation to ban smoking at state colleges and universities.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-15) He co-sponsored a bill to create an [earned income tax credit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_income_tax_credit "Earned income tax credit").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-16) He was a supporter of LGBT rights as early as 2002.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-17) During his tenure, he served on the Judiciary Committee.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-18)

## Connecticut State Senate (2003–2007)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Connecticut State Senate (2003–2007)")]

### Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Elections")]

After two terms in the Connecticut House, Murphy ran for a seat in the [Connecticut State Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_State_Senate "Connecticut State Senate") in 2002. The open 16th district had been held by a Republican for more than a decade. In [the general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Connecticut_Senate_election "2002 Connecticut Senate election"), he defeated Republican State Representative [Ann Dandrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dandrow "Ann Dandrow"), 53%–47%.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-19) He was reelected in 2004, defeating Republican Christopher O'Brien, 60%–37%.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-20)

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Tenure")]

In 2003, Murphy joined the Clean Car Alliance and supported California-like environmental standards on auto manufacturers.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-21)

In 2004, Murphy supported a bill to ban smoking in restaurants and bars.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-23)

In 2005, Murphy authored legislation establishing the new Office of Child Protection, to "better coordinate advocacy for abused and neglected children".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-24) Murphy also wrote Public Act 05–149, an act permitting [stem-cell research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem-cell_research "Stem-cell research") while prohibiting human cloning.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-26) The act, signed into law by Governor [Jodi Rell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodi_Rell "Jodi Rell"), made Connecticut the third state in the nation to permit taxpayer-subsidized stem-cell research.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-27)

During his tenure in the State Senate, Murphy was one of the first ten co-sponsors of a [civil union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_union "Civil union") bill that passed the General Assembly in 2005. On his Senate campaign website, Murphy summarized his stance: "Let me be clear and simple: LGBT rights are human rights. Marriage equality and nondiscrimination in the military, workplace, classroom and healthcare system, based on real or perceived sexual orientation and gender identity, are civil rights that must be protected under law."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-28) During his tenure he chaired the Public Health Committee.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-29)

He was reelected in 2008 and 2010 with 60% and 54% of the vote, respectively.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-33)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Tenure")]

Murphy has received high ratings from progressive groups such as [Americans for Democratic Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans_for_Democratic_Action "Americans for Democratic Action"), [NARAL Pro-Choice America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NARAL_Pro-Choice_America "NARAL Pro-Choice America"), and various labor unions; and low scores from conservative groups as the [Club for Growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_for_Growth "Club for Growth"), [American Conservative Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Conservative_Union "American Conservative Union"), and [FreedomWorks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FreedomWorks "FreedomWorks").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-34)

In 2008, Murphy sent [House Majority Leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaders_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives "Leaders of the United States House of Representatives")[Steny Hoyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steny_Hoyer "Steny Hoyer") a letter expressing support for increased oil drilling as part of a bipartisan energy bill.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-35)

Murphy supports reform of federal supportive housing programs, which assist low-income people with severe disabilities. In 2008, the House of Representatives passed the "Frank Melville Supportive Housing Investment Act", which Murphy authored to modernize and streamline Section 811, which governs federal supportive housing grants.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-36)

Murphy has called for the closure of the [Guantanamo Bay detention camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_detention_camp "Guantanamo Bay detention camp"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-37) but in 2011, he voted to extend provisions of the [Patriot Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot_Act "Patriot Act").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-38)

#### Health care reform

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Health care reform")]

In 2009, Murphy helped draft [HR 3200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HR_3200 "HR 3200"), the House health-care reform bill. Murphy defended his role in supporting the bill at a contentious town hall meeting in [Simsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simsbury,_Connecticut "Simsbury, Connecticut") in August 2009.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-40)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Ted_Kennedy_at_Barack_Obama_rally_2%2C_February_4%2C_2008.jpg/250px-Ted_Kennedy_at_Barack_Obama_rally_2%2C_February_4%2C_2008.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ted_Kennedy_at_Barack_Obama_rally_2,_February_4,_2008.jpg)

[Ted Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy "Ted Kennedy") and Murphy at a Barack Obama rally in February 2008

A longtime supporter of health insurance reform, Murphy is a strong proponent of the [public option](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_option "Public option"), which entails the creation of an independent, government-sponsored health insurance plan to compete with private companies. He has argued that such a plan would not require government financing and would help introduce competition into monopolized health insurance markets and help reduce costs.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-41)

#### Congressional and judicial ethics reform

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Congressional and judicial ethics reform")]

In May 2007, Murphy organized a group of freshman House members to support the creation of an independent, nonpartisan ethics panel to review complaints filed against House members.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-42) He has been credited with helping to shape the independent [Office of Congressional Ethics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Congressional_Ethics "Office of Congressional Ethics"), which was passed into law by the House in March 2008.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-43)

Murphy sponsored a bill that would subject [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") justices to the same ethical code that applies to other federal judges and suggested in 2011 the possibility of an investigation of whether Justice [Clarence Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_Thomas "Clarence Thomas") had committed ethical violations that would justify removing him from office. The matter in question was Thomas's connection to Harlan Crow[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-44) and other supporters of the Republican Party.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-45) Murphy circulated a draft letter to other members of Congress asking the House Judiciary Committee leadership to hold a hearing on the Supreme Court Transparency and Disclosure Act, which would end the Supreme Court's immunity to judicial ethics laws.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-46)

As a member of the [House Oversight and Government Reform Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Oversight_and_Accountability "United States House Committee on Oversight and Accountability"), Murphy was highly critical of for-profit government contractors operating in Iraq, which functioned with little government oversight and scrutiny. He introduced the Government Funding Transparency Act of 2008, which required private companies that do the majority of their business with the federal government to publicly disclose their top executives' salaries.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-47)

Two home invasions occurred in Murphy's district in 2007 and 2008; the latter, in Cheshire, was especially brutal, with the rape and murder of a mother and her two daughters. In response, Murphy proposed making home invasion a federal crime.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-48)

Murphy has been a proponent of the proposed [New Haven-Hartford-Springfield Commuter Rail Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven-Hartford-Springfield_Commuter_Rail_Line "New Haven-Hartford-Springfield Commuter Rail Line"), an effort to use existing [Amtrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amtrak "Amtrak") railroad tracks for daily commuter service on par with Southwestern Connecticut's [Metro-North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-North "Metro-North") service into New York. In 2008, Murphy successfully added an amendment to rail legislation making it easier for Amtrak and the state of Connecticut to cooperate on the rail project.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-49) The line began operation in 2018.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-50)

Murphy proposed reforms of the nation's "missing persons" databases, introducing "Billy's Law" in 2009 to improve coordination of law-enforcement efforts to find missing persons. The legislation was named in honor of Billy Smolinski Jr., a onetime resident of Murphy's district who disappeared in 2004.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-51)

Murphy took office as the junior United States senator for Connecticut on January 3, 2013. In the Senate, he has worked on funding for transportation and infrastructure, the preservation of Long Island Sound, growing small farms and promoting Connecticut manufacturing.

In 2016, Murphy walked 126 miles across Connecticut, listening to constituents and holding daily town hall meetings.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-66) He repeated the walk in 2017, covering 106 miles and holding five town hall meetings.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-67)

In early 2020, Murphy secretly[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-68) met with Iranian foreign minister [Javad Zarif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javad_Zarif "Javad Zarif") on the sidelines of [Munich Security Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_Security_Conference "Munich Security Conference"). They discussed [U.S. nationals being detained in Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_foreign_nationals_detained_in_Iran "List of foreign nationals detained in Iran"), [Iran's involvement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Saudi_Arabia_proxy_conflict "Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict") in the [Yemeni Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemeni_Civil_War_(2014%E2%80%93present) "Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)"), and [Iranian-backed militias in Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_intervention_in_Iraq_(2014%E2%80%93present) "Iranian intervention in Iraq (2014–present)"). In a post on [Medium.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium.com "Medium.com"), Murphy wrote: "I have no delusions about Iran—they are our adversary, responsible for the killing of thousands of Americans and unacceptable levels of support for terrorist organizations throughout the Middle East. But I think it's dangerous to not talk to your enemies. Discussions and negotiations are a way to ease tensions and reduce the chances for crisis."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-69)

In the wake of the [January 6 United States Capitol attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack") in 2021, Murphy called for the [removal of Donald Trump from office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_impeachment_of_Donald_Trump "Second impeachment of Donald Trump").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-70) He also said he would lead an investigation into the security breaches and law enforcement response during the attack.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-Seldin-71)

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Political positions")]

Murphy has been generally regarded as a mainstream [liberal Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_liberalism_in_the_United_States "Modern liberalism in the United States"), but in the 2020s, he has become a prominent advocate of [left-leaning economic populism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-wing_populism "Left-wing populism"), urging Democrats to adopt an "aggressively populist" message to win back [working-class voters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_class_in_the_United_States "Working class in the United States").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-82) Murphy is a member of the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate "U.S. Senate")'s [Fight Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight_Club_(U.S._Senate) "Fight Club (U.S. Senate)").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-83)

While historically known for his expertise on foreign policy, gun control advocacy, and bipartisan negotiating skills, Murphy has recently focused on aggressively opposing [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and his perceived authoritarianism, and addressing what he calls a "crisis of meaning" in U.S. society and an identity crisis among American men.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-87)

### Abortion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Abortion")]

Murphy is [pro-choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_abortion-rights_movement "United States abortion-rights movement"). When _[Roe v. Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roe\_v.\_Wade "Roe v. Wade")_[was overturned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dobbs_v._Jackson_Women's_Health_Organization "Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization") in June 2022, Murphy called it a "disaster".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-Tweet1-88)

### Economic issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Economic issues")]

Murphy has introduced two pieces of legislation, the American Jobs Matter Act[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-89) and the 21st Century Buy American Act,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-90) to close loopholes in the existing [Buy American laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buy_American_Act "Buy American Act") and encourage the U.S. government to purchase [American-made goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Made_in_USA "Made in USA").

In May 2018, Murphy was one of 12 senators to sign a letter to [Federal Labor Relations Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Labor_Relations_Authority "Federal Labor Relations Authority") (FLRA) chair [Colleen Kiko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colleen_Kiko "Colleen Kiko") urging the FLRA to end efforts to close its Boston regional office until Congress debated the matter, adding that the FLRA's closure of its regional offices would cause staff to be placed farther away from the federal employees whose rights they protect.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-91)

Murphy has spoken out against outsourcing.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-92) He has been an outspoken critic of [neoliberalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoliberalism "Neoliberalism") since 2022 and has instead advocated [big-tent politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_tent_politics "Big tent politics") and [left-wing populism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-wing_populism "Left-wing populism") to win back working-class voters and build a winning coalition.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-94)

After [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") lost the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), Murphy urged a significant revamp of Democratic Party policy, saying that [neoliberalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoliberalism "Neoliberalism"), growing social and economic alienation of many Americans from the party, and a perception of [elitism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elitism "Elitism") have contributed to the party's loss of working class voters. Murphy believes the Democratic Party should embrace [left-wing populism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-wing_populism "Left-wing populism") as an antidote to [right-wing populism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-wing_populism "Right-wing populism"), reiterating that [Third Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Way "Third Way") economic policies have eroded the party's once broad appeal.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-95)

Murphy was one of the first members of Congress to come out in opposition to [US support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._support_for_Saudi-led_operations_in_Yemen "U.S. support for Saudi-led operations in Yemen") for the [Saudi-led military campaign in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian-led_intervention_in_Yemen "Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen"), which was launched in 2015.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-96) In a speech on January 29, 2016, he recommended that the US stop supporting this campaign and suspend military sales to [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") until it received assurances that the war would not distract from Saudi efforts against [al-Qaeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda "Al-Qaeda") and [ISIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISIS "ISIS") and Saudi Arabia reduced its worldwide support of [Wahhabism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wahhabism "Wahhabism").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-97)

Murphy is a member of the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Foreign_Relations_Committee "Senate Foreign Relations Committee") and the ranking Democratic member of the subcommittee on the Middle East and Counter-terrorism.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-98) In June 8, 2015, edition of _[Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign\_Affairs "Foreign Affairs")_, Murphy co-authored "Principles for a Progressive Foreign Policy", proposing a framework for a Democratic foreign policy strategy.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-99)

In November 2017, Murphy accused the United States of complicity in the [war crimes committed in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_violations_during_the_Yemeni_Civil_War_(2015-present) "Human rights violations during the Yemeni Civil War (2015-present)") by the Saudi-led military coalition and in [Yemen's humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famine_in_Yemen "Famine in Yemen"), saying: "Thousands and thousands inside Yemen today are dying....This horror is caused in part by our decision to facilitate a bombing campaign that is murdering children and to endorse a Saudi strategy inside Yemen that is deliberately using disease and starvation and the withdrawal of humanitarian support as a tactic."[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-100) In October 2018, Murphy wrote that if the reports of [Jamal Khashoggi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_Khashoggi "Jamal Khashoggi")'s [murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_Jamal_Khashoggi "Murder of Jamal Khashoggi") were true, "it should represent a fundamental break" in [Saudi Arabia–United States relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia%E2%80%93United_States_relations "Saudi Arabia–United States relations").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-101) Murphy, [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders"), and [Mike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Lee "Mike Lee") advanced a vote to co-sponsor a resolution that would require the President to "withdraw troops in or "affecting" Yemen within 30 days unless they are fighting al Qaeda.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-102) In February 2019, Murphy was one of seven senators to reintroduce legislation requiring sanctions on Saudi officials involved in Khashoggi's murder and seeking to address support for the Yemen civil war by prohibiting some weapons sales to Saudi Arabia and U.S. military refueling of Saudi coalition planes.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-103)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Chris_Murphy_and_Sven_Mikser_%2837165237034%29.jpg/250px-Chris_Murphy_and_Sven_Mikser_%2837165237034%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chris_Murphy_and_Sven_Mikser_(37165237034).jpg)

Murphy with Estonian Foreign Minister [Sven Mikser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven_Mikser "Sven Mikser") in 2016

Murphy is one of the Senate's most vociferous critics of Russia. Murphy holds that Russia will remain a permanent, persistent threat to the United States and its security interests regardless of the incumbent regime in the country. At a 2019 event at the [Atlantic Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Council "Atlantic Council"), Murphy professed the need for [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") allies to understand that the US has been always "far behind Russia in understanding our vulnerabilities".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-auto-104) At the same event, Murphy echoed the sentiments of Lithuanian and Georgian foreign ministers that Russia's imperialist nature will always put it at odds with the US and that little will change until Russia as a "captive state of aggregate territories" changes its nature.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-auto-104)

In March 2016, Murphy and Republican Senator [Rob Portman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Portman "Rob Portman") co-authored the bipartisan [Countering Foreign Propaganda and Disinformation Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countering_Foreign_Propaganda_and_Disinformation_Act "Countering Foreign Propaganda and Disinformation Act").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-combatpropaganda-105) Congressman [Adam Kinzinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kinzinger "Adam Kinzinger") introduced the House version of the bill.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-house-106) After the [2016 U.S. presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election"), worries grew that propaganda spread and organized by the [Russian government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_government "Russian government") swayed the election's outcome, and members of Congress took action to safeguard the [national security of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security_of_the_United_States "National security of the United States") by advancing legislation to monitor propaganda from external threats.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-combatpropaganda-105)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-representativesbacks-107) On November 30, 2016, legislators approved a measure within the [National Defense Authorization Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defense_Authorization_Act "National Defense Authorization Act") to ask the [U.S. State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") to take action against foreign propaganda through an interagency panel.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-combatpropaganda-105)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-representativesbacks-107) The legislation authorized funding of $160 million over two years.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-combatpropaganda-105) The initiative was developed through the Countering Foreign Propaganda and Disinformation Act.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-combatpropaganda-105)

In September 2016, in advance of [UN Security Council resolution 2334](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2334 "United Nations Security Council Resolution 2334") condemning [Israeli settlements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlement "Israeli settlement") in the occupied [Palestinian territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_territories "Palestinian territories"), Murphy signed an [AIPAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIPAC "AIPAC")-sponsored letter urging President Obama to veto "one-sided" resolutions against Israel.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-108)

In July 2017, Murphy voted in favor of the [Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countering_America's_Adversaries_Through_Sanctions_Act "Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act") that placed [sanctions on Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_sanctions_against_Iran "United States sanctions against Iran"), Russia, and [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-110)

In December 2017, Murphy criticized President Trump's decision to [recognize Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_recognition_of_Jerusalem_as_capital_of_Israel "United States recognition of Jerusalem as capital of Israel") as the capital of Israel, saying, "It needs to be done at the right time and in the right manner."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-111)

In December 2018, Trump ordered the [withdrawal of U.S. troops from Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-led_intervention_in_the_Syrian_Civil_War "American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War"). Murphy said: "I support withdrawing troops, but we must also rejoin a diplomatic process that the Trump administration has left to other powers, and we need a surge in humanitarian relief. That's the only way we can protect the Syrian people against a [Turkish incursion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_involvement_in_the_Syrian_Civil_War "Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War") or regime reprisals.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-112)

In April 2019, Murphy was one of 34 senators to sign a letter to President Trump encouraging him "to listen to members of your own Administration and reverse a decision that will damage our national security and aggravate conditions inside Central America", asserting that Trump had "consistently expressed a flawed understanding of U.S. foreign assistance" since becoming president and that he was "personally undermining efforts to promote U.S. national security and economic prosperity" by preventing the use of Fiscal Year 2018 national security funding. The senators argued that foreign assistance to Central American countries created less migration to the U.S. by helping to improve conditions in those countries.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-113)

In January 2020, Murphy wrote to [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") Director [Christopher A. Wray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_A._Wray "Christopher A. Wray"), urging the FBI to "investigate the allegations" that [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") "illegally compromised and stole personal data" from [Jeff Bezos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos"), the owner of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_, as part of a possible effort to "influence, if not silence, the _Washington Post'_ s reporting on Saudi Arabia".[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-115)

In May 2020, Murphy voiced his opposition to Israel's plan to [annex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposed_Israeli_annexation_of_the_West_Bank "Proposed Israeli annexation of the West Bank") parts of the Israeli-occupied [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-116)

In January 2024, Murphy voted against a resolution proposed by Senator [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders") to apply the [human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_violations_against_Palestinians_by_Israel "Human rights violations against Palestinians by Israel") provisions of the [Foreign Assistance Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Assistance_Act "Foreign Assistance Act") to [U.S. aid to Israel's military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_support_for_Israel_in_the_Gaza_war "United States support for Israel in the Gaza war"). The proposal was defeated, 72 to 11.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-117) On February 7, 2024, Murphy said he would support an amendment requiring weapons sold internationally to be used in compliance with U.S. law, international humanitarian law, and the laws of armed conflict.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-118)

In March 2024, Murphy was one of 19 Democratic senators to sign a letter to the Biden administration urging the U.S. to recognize a "nonmilitarized" [Palestinian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Palestine "State of Palestine") after the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-119)

In March 2025, Murphy said, "The White House has become an arm of the Kremlin."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-120)

In April 2025, Murphy voted for a pair of resolutions, proposed by Sanders, to cancel the [Trump's administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump")'s sales of $8.8 billion in bombs and other munitions to Israel. The proposals were defeated, 82 to 15.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-121)

In June 2025, after Trump made remarks about bombing Iranian nuclear facilities, Murphy told reporters, "It appears that we have only delayed Iran's nuclear program by a few months. The president's assertions that we have dismantled the program are false. Knowledge cannot be eradicated through bombing."[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-122)

Murphy has criticized the Trump administration's handling of the [2026 Iran war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war "2026 Iran war"), calling its strategy "incoherent", "bungled", and "mismanaged". He also argued that the administration had bypassed Congress in initiating military action against Iran and introduced a War Powers Resolution aimed at limiting U.S. involvement in unauthorized hostilities against Iran.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-125) Murphy also linked the conflict to rising fuel prices and broader economic pressures in the United States.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-126)

Following reports of a U.S.–Iran memorandum of understanding in June 2026, Murphy questioned its legitimacy, saying he had not been briefed on its contents and expressing uncertainty about whether it formally existed. He called the reported agreement favorable to Iran and "essentially a surrender", while criticizing the lack of transparency toward Congress.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-127)

### Gun control

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Gun control")]

Further information: [Chris Murphy gun control filibuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_gun_control_filibuster "Chris Murphy gun control filibuster")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Chris_Murphy_Gun_Control_%2834368843553%29.jpg/250px-Chris_Murphy_Gun_Control_%2834368843553%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chris_Murphy_Gun_Control_(34368843553).jpg)

Murphy speaks in favor of gun control in 2017.

Murphy supports gun control and has been a leading advocate for further legislation relating to it.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-128) He supports a national assault-weapon ban and introduced such a ban in 2017 and 2023.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-weaponban-129)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-senatejoins-130) Murphy has an F rating with the [NRA Political Victory Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRA_Political_Victory_Fund "NRA Political Victory Fund") and in 2020 published a book on gun control, _The Violence Inside Us: A Brief History of an Ongoing American Tragedy._[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-131)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-votesmart-ratings-132)

The [Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandy_Hook_Elementary_School_shooting "Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting") occurred in [Newtown, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newtown,_Connecticut "Newtown, Connecticut"), in Murphy's House district near the end of his term. In the aftermath of the shooting, he became a leading voice in the movement to prevent gun violence, supporting numerous policies, including universal background checks and ending the ban on gun violence research at the [CDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control_and_Prevention "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-133) Murphy supported the bipartisan Manchin-Toomey background checks proposal, which would have strengthened and expanded the existing background-check system and established a National Commission on Mass Violence to study in-depth all the causes of mass violence.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-134) When the proposal failed to meet the 60-vote threshold for advancement, Murphy said, "This is a day when the Republican filibuster stood in the way of 90% of Americans."[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-135)

In his first month in office, he criticized the [National Rifle Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Rifle_Association "National Rifle Association") and [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") for a video game involving shooting with guns that was labeled appropriate for children as young as four.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-136)

On June 24, 2015, Murphy said, "Since Sandy Hook there has been a [school shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_shooting "School shooting"), on average, every week"; _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ called this statement misleading.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-137) On June 15–16, 2016, Murphy staged a filibuster regarding gun control following the [Orlando nightclub shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_nightclub_shooting "Orlando nightclub shooting"), the deadliest [mass shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_shooting "Mass shooting") in U.S. history at the time. The filibuster entered the list of the top 10 longest filibusters in U.S. history.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-138) In the wake of the shooting, Murphy said, "This phenomenon of near-constant mass shootings happens only in America—nowhere else" and "this epidemic will continue without end if Congress continues to sit on its hands and do nothing—again."[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-Berkowitz61616-139)

After the 2017 [Sutherland Springs church shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutherland_Springs_church_shooting "Sutherland Springs church shooting"), Murphy and Senator [John Cornyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cornyn "John Cornyn") introduced the bipartisan [Fix NICS Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fix_NICS_Act_of_2017 "Fix NICS Act of 2017") to ensure criminal records are submitted to the federal background-check system. The legislation passed in the [2018 Consolidated Appropriations Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_Appropriations_Act,_2018 "Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2018").[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-140)

After the 2018 [Stoneman Douglas High School shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoneman_Douglas_High_School_shooting "Stoneman Douglas High School shooting"),[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-141) Murphy made an impassioned call for action in the Senate, saying, "this happens nowhere else other than the United States of America, this epidemic of mass slaughter, this scourge of school shooting after school shooting. It only happens here not because of coincidence, not because of bad luck, but as a consequence of our inaction. We are responsible for a level of mass atrocity that happens in this country with zero parallel anywhere else. As a parent it scares me to death that this body doesn't take seriously the safety of my children, and it seems like a lot of parents in South Florida will be asking the same question today. We pray for families, for the victims. We hope for the best."[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-142) In March 2018, Murphy was one of ten senators to sign a letter to [Senate HELP Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Health,_Education,_Labor_and_Pensions "United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions") chair [Lamar Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_Alexander "Lamar Alexander") and ranking Democrat [Patty Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patty_Murray "Patty Murray") requesting they schedule a hearing on the causes and remedies of mass shootings in the wake of the shooting.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-143)

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ec/Senator_Chris_Murphy_on_the_Assassination_of_Charlie_Kirk.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Murphy addresses the [assassination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Charlie_Kirk "Assassination of Charlie Kirk") of conservative activist [Charlie Kirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Kirk "Charlie Kirk") before speaking on the Senate floor; September 10, 2025.

After the [Robb Elementary School Shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robb_Elementary_School_Shooting "Robb Elementary School Shooting"), Murphy emerged as the lead Democratic negotiator in support of the [Bipartisan Safer Communities Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipartisan_Safer_Communities_Act "Bipartisan Safer Communities Act").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-144) The act, which would partially close the [Boyfriend loophole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyfriend_loophole "Boyfriend loophole") while providing federal funding for mental health and [red flag law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_flag_law "Red flag law") adaptation, was viewed as the first piece of notable gun-safety legislation in decades.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-146) This bill passed with a bipartisan Senate majority and is considered highly significant gun-violence legislation.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-147)

### Health care

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Health care")]

Murphy has been a leading Senate supporter of the [Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act") and has opposed Republican attempts to repeal it, consistently speaking on the floor about its favorable effects on his constituents.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-148)

In April 2017, Murphy was one of five Democratic senators to sign a letter to President Trump that warned that failure "to take immediate action to oppose the lawsuit or direct House Republicans to forgo this effort will increase instability in the insurance market, as insurers may choose not to participate in the marketplace in 2018" and that they remained concerned that his administration "has still not provided certainty to insurers and consumers that you will protect the cost-sharing subsidies provided under the law."[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-149)

Murphy called the American Health Care Act of 2017 "an intellectual and moral dumpster fire" that would cause 24 million Americans to lose their health insurance.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-150)

In 2021, Murphy co-sponsored senator [Jeff Merkley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Merkley "Jeff Merkley")'s Choose Medicare Act,[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-151) which, according to Murphy's Senate webpage, would have allowed "every American and every American business to buy into Medicare".[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-152) While commenting on [Abdul El-Sayed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdul_El-Sayed "Abdul El-Sayed")'s victory in the Democratic primary for the [2026 United States Senate election in Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_Michigan "2026 United States Senate election in Michigan") and asked about El-Sayed's support for [Medicare for All](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-payer_healthcare "Single-payer healthcare"), Murphy said, "everyone in [America] should have access to the Medicare plan".[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-153)

#### Mental health

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Mental health")]

On August 5, 2015, Murphy and Republican Senator [Bill Cassidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cassidy "Bill Cassidy") introduced the bipartisan Mental Health Reform Act of 2015. The legislation, aimed at overhauling the mental health system, would build treatment capacity, promote integrated care models, expand the mental health workforce, and encourage the enforcement of existing mental health parity laws.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-154)

The bill was informed by listening sessions that Murphy conducted across Connecticut.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-155) The bill was widely supported by the mental health community, with organizations including the [American Psychiatric Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Psychiatric_Association "American Psychiatric Association"),[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-156) Mental Health America[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-157) and the National Council for Behavioral Health[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-158) applauding its introduction.

On March 16, 2016, the Mental Health Reform Act was unanimously passed by the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee. On December 7, 2016, the Senate passed the act as a part of the [21st Century Cures Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st_Century_Cures_Act "21st Century Cures Act"). The bill also provided $1 billion to address the opioid crisis and funding for the [NIH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institutes_of_Health "National Institutes of Health") Cancer Moonshot initiative. President Obama signed the bill into law on December 13, 2016.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-159)

### LGBTQ rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: LGBTQ rights")]

On September 18, 2024, Murphy opposed a Republican resolution banning trans girls from participating in girls' sports. He pointed out that Florida had banned trans girls from girls' sports when, of 800,000 high-school athletes in the state, only 13 had been known to be trans girls. He said that keeping trans kids out of sports "isn't an effort to solve a problem...I celebrate the fact that they get the experience of the camaraderie and the happiness that comes with being part of a sports team. I think that's great, and I don't think that is a threat to my kids. I don't think that's a threat to my community or my nation." He rebuked Republicans for their "obsession with transgender kids".[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-160)

### Loneliness and social connection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Loneliness and social connection")]

Murphy has been a vocal advocate for addressing [loneliness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loneliness_epidemic "Loneliness epidemic") in America, an issue he has framed as both a [public health crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_crisis "Health crisis") and a societal challenge that requires immediate, bipartisan action.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:0-161)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:1-162)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:2-163) He has called loneliness a "[spiritual crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiritual_crisis "Spiritual crisis")"[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:3-164) that fuels increased addiction, violence, and suicide[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:4-165)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:0-161)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:3-164) across [demographics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demography "Demography"), regions, and [partisan lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_(politics) "Partisan (politics)"). He makes the case that genuine happiness and [well-being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-being "Well-being") are closely tied to [social connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_connection "Social connection") rather than solely [economic success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wealth "Wealth"), emphasizing the importance of policies that encourage community and [family bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family "Family").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:5-166)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:0-161)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:3-164)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:6-167) In an op-ed co-written with [Richard Weissbourd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Weissbourd "Richard Weissbourd"), Murphy argued that America's overemphasis on [individualism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individualism "Individualism") has led to a cultural shift away from collective welfare, making it critical to restore a balance between individual success and the "[common good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_good "Common good")".[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:1-162)

In July 2023, Murphy introduced the National Strategy for Social Connection Act, which aims to establish a [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") Office of Social Connection Policy.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:7-168)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:0-161) The office's purpose is to coordinate with [federal agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_agency "Government agency") to create policies promoting social infrastructure and issue guidelines to foster social bonds.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:2-163)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-169) The proposed legislation also suggests funding for the [CDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control_and_Prevention "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention") to research loneliness and [social isolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_isolation "Social isolation"), highlighting the health risks associated with [disconnection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_detachment "Emotional detachment"), such as increased [susceptibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susceptible_individual "Susceptible individual") to [heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiovascular_disease "Cardiovascular disease") and [dementia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dementia "Dementia").[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:0-161)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:3-164)

Murphy has sought to generate bipartisan support for his efforts to address loneliness. In April 2024, in partnership with the [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)")[Governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States) "Governor (United States)") of [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah")[Spencer Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Cox "Spencer Cox"), Murphy announced a series of round-table events about restoring the value of the common good.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:6-167) Described as "a national effort to convene discussions", these forums were intended to bring together thinkers, researchers, and writers on the left and right to explore community solutions to combat loneliness and foster [social solidarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solidarity "Solidarity").[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:3-164)

Murphy has also proposed targeted measures such as regulating youth access to social media, improving labor policies to allow more [leisure time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leisure "Leisure"), and supporting institutions like trade unions and [religious organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_organization "Religious organization") that naturally build community.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:7-168)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:3-164) His goal is to reframe policy discussions around social well-being, and rebuild the "[social fabric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_system "Social system")" weakened by modern [individualism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individualism "Individualism") and [technological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technology "Technology")[isolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_isolation "Social isolation").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:5-166)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:4-165)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:6-167)

In January 2025, Murphy and Senators [Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz"), [Katie Britt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Britt "Katie Britt"), and [Brian Schatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Schatz "Brian Schatz") introduced the [Kids Off Social Media Act (KOSMA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kids_Off_Social_Media_Act "Kids Off Social Media Act"). Senators [John Curtis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Curtis "John Curtis"), [Peter Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Welch "Peter Welch"), [John Fetterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fetterman "John Fetterman"), [Ted Budd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Budd "Ted Budd"), [Mark Warner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Warner "Mark Warner"), and [Angus King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angus_King "Angus King") co-sponsored the act.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-170) It would set a minimum age of 13 to use social media platforms and prevent social media companies from feeding "algorithmically targeted" content to users under 17. Murphy said, "Everyone knows how harmful social media can be to kids. As a parent, I've seen firsthand how these platforms use intentionally addictive algorithms to spoon-feed young people horrifying content glorifying everything from suicide to eating disorders. Yet these companies have proven they will choose profits over the well-being of our kids unless we force them to do otherwise. This bipartisan legislation will finally hold social media companies accountable".[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-171)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-172)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-173)

### Immigration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Immigration")]

In July 2019, Murphy and 15 other Senate Democrats introduced the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which mandated that ICE agents obtain a supervisor's approval before engaging in enforcement actions at sensitive locations, except in special circumstances; that agents receive annual training; and that they annually report enforcement actions in those locations.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-174)

Murphy co-wrote and negotiated support for the [Bipartisan Border Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico%E2%80%93United_States_border_crisis#2024_bipartisan_border_bill "Mexico–United States border crisis"), also called the Border Act of 2024, which did not pass.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-175)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-177)

### U.S. Supreme Court

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: U.S. Supreme Court")]

After the U.S. Supreme Court overturned _[Roe v. Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roe\_v.\_Wade "Roe v. ## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chris_Murphy&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Murphy married Catherine Holahan in August 2007.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:8-179) After 17 years of marriage, they separated in November 2024 and divorced in July 2026.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-181) They have two sons together.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:8-179) In September 2025, [Semafor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semafor_(website) "Semafor (website)") reported that Murphy was dating [Tara McGowan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tara_McGowan "Tara McGowan"), an American political strategist. They were no longer dating by October of that year.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:9-65) Raised as a [Congregationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregationalist "Congregationalist"), Murphy identifies as "unspecified/other Protestant" but said in 2015 that he was "not a regular churchgoer these days, in part because of kids, in part because of a busy schedule."[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-182) By 2023, Murphy had joined churches in Hartford and Washington.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:0-161)

Every year, Murphy walks across a different route of the entire state of Connecticut, to meet and reacquaint himself with his constituents.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_(politician)#cite_note-:9-65)
